name: Texas

rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Sept. 1, 1993 needs a boater education certificate to run a PWC, a motorboat over 15 hp or a sailboat over 14 ft.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de septiembre de 1993 o después necesita el certificado de educación náutica para manejar una moto acuática, una lancha de más de 15 hp o un velero de más de 14 pies.

minAge.note: Alone from 13 (motor over 15 hp, PWC, sailboat over 14 ft) with the course; under 13 needs a legal operator 18+ on board.

exemptions: Accompanied by a legal operator 18+ on board.
A one-time 15-day deferral can be bought where hunting and fishing licenses are sold.

card.feeNote: TPWD says course fees start at $10 and vary by provider and format.

nonResident: Visitors follow Texas rules; NASBLA-approved certificates from any state or US territory are accepted.

sources.quote: You must complete a Texas Boater Education Certification Course if you were born on or after September 1, 1993 , and will be operating: A personal watercraft (PWC) A motorboat with more than 15 horsepower A sailboat over 14 feet
To operate a vessel alone in Texas, a boater must be 13 years of age to operate a vessel of more than 15 horsepower; a PWC, or windblown vessel over 14 feet in length
Fees start at $10 for a basic course and varies depending on in-person or online courses.
A person may purchase a one-time 15 day boater education deferral at any place hunting and fishing licenses are sold.
Texas does recognize and accept NASBLA approved state courses from all 50 states and the US territories.
